body: Video timelines are opaque binaries: change one frame and you re-render everything. There is nothing to read, review, or diff — the motion is locked inside the file.
sections.caption: A sealed timeline: one frame changes, everything re-renders.
sections.title: Timelines are opaque

body: emaki scenes are JSON: components, tracks and timing as data. A scene is a file you can read, diff in a pull request, and generate from code.
sections.caption: Components, tracks and timing as JSON.
sections.title: Scenes as data

body: One set of scenes renders as article figures, a story player, and narrated video. Write the motion once, and publish it everywhere it needs to be.
sections.caption: One scene file wired to three renders.
sections.title: One source, three renders

takeaway: Motion you can review like code.
